prompt.context: Rock Energy, an Oil & Gas company, is evaluating the purchase of one of three oil fields in Latin America. After purchasing the rights to extract oil from one of these fields, Rock Energy will outsource the drilling activity.
prompt.question: How would you evaluate the three oil fields, and which oil field should Rock Energy purchase?

clarifying_info.q: How long do the drilling rights last and when does production start?
clarifying_info.a: The rights give Rock Energy the right to drill during Year 1 and produce oil for 20 years. Assume no oil is produced until the beginning of Year 2.

clarifying_info.q: How many rigs can be deployed in each region?
clarifying_info.a: Rock Energy can get the drilling operator to deploy a maximum of 10 rigs in each region.

clarifying_info.q: What does the rig day cost include?
clarifying_info.a: The cost per rig day includes crew, consumables, and services.
Any amount of oil extracted will be sold at the spot market price of the moment.

clarifying_info.q: Are there maintenance costs during the 20-year production period?
clarifying_info.a: For simplicity, assume the oil wells produce the same amount of oil for the next 20 years with no maintenance costs.

clarifying_info.q: What is the cost to acquire the rights in each region?
clarifying_info.a: The rights to extract oil cost $40M in each region.

exhibits.title: Oil Field Profiles, 2010
exhibits.shows: A comparison table of three regions showing drilling rates (meters/day), average depth of wells (meters), number of rigs that would operate, average well production (barrels per day), and cost per rig day. A note states wells are continuously dug for only one year and rigs move to a new well once the current one is completed.

framework: Calculate days to drill one well per region: Depth / Penetration Rate
Calculate cost per well: Days to drill x Cost per rig day
Calculate yearly revenue per well: Daily production x 360 days x Spot price
Calculate profit per well and profit margin per well
Calculate number of wells drillable per year per region: (360 / Days per well) x Number of rigs
Calculate Total Revenue, Total Cost (drilling + rights acquisition), and Total Profit per region
Compare regions and select highest-profit option
Assess qualitative risks that could affect the investment decision

questions.prompt: What are the first-year profits for each region (Year 1 = drilling, production begins Year 2)?
questions.guidance: Candidate should walk through the full calculation for all three regions: drilling time, cost per well, revenue per well, number of wells, then aggregate profit. Key insight: Region 2 wins despite a lower per-well margin than Region 1 because the number of wells drilled is large enough and fixed costs are spread over more wells. Region 3 is unprofitable due to deep wells and high cost.

math.setup: Spot price = $50/barrel. Year assumed to be 360 days. Up to 10 rigs per region. Rights cost $40M per region.
steps: Days to drill one well: R1 = 1200/20 = 60 days; R2 = 2700/30 = 90 days; R3 = 3600/20 = 180 days
Yearly production per well (barrels): R1 = 100 x 360 = 36,000; R2 = 200 x 360 = 72,000; R3 = 300 x 360 = 108,000
Profit margin per well: R1 = 500%; R2 = 300%; R3 = 50%
math.answer: Region 1 profit = $50M; Region 2 profit = $68M; Region 3 profit = -$4M. Region 2 is the most profitable.

brainstorming.prompt: What qualitative factors and risks should Rock Energy consider before finalizing the investment decision?

categories.name: Insurance & Liability
ideas: Countries have different regulations on required insurance coverage for Oil & Gas operations
Liability caps vary by country, directly affecting insurance costs
Deep-water or politically volatile regions may require higher premiums

categories.name: Political Risk
ideas: Accessing a well site can become difficult in politically unstable regions
Property rights may not be reliably enforced
Government expropriation or contract renegotiation risk
Export restrictions or windfall taxes could reduce realized revenue

categories.name: Labor
ideas: Labor contracts and union power differ by country
Strikes or work stoppages could delay drilling timelines
Local content requirements may restrict access to cheaper international crews

categories.name: Oil Price Volatility
ideas: Prices below $27/barrel would make all three regions have a negative return
Long 20-year production horizon means significant price uncertainty
Hedging instruments (futures, options) could mitigate downside

categories.name: Oil Quality
ideas: Differences in crude quality (API gravity, sulfur content) can affect the realized spot price
Heavy or sour crude may trade at a discount to benchmark prices
Refinery compatibility in the region may affect offtake options

recommendation: Rock Energy should purchase the drilling rights for Region 2
Region 2 yields the highest total first-year profit of $68M, compared to $50M for Region 1 and a loss of $4M for Region 3
Although Region 1 has a higher per-well profit margin (500% vs 300%), Region 2 drills 40 wells generating substantially more total revenue and profit after the fixed $40M rights cost
risks: Oil prices below $27/barrel would result in negative returns across all regions
Political instability in the Latin American region could disrupt site access or property rights
Higher insurance obligations in certain countries could erode profitability
Oil quality differences could cause Region 2's realized price to differ from the $50 spot price assumed
next_steps: Conduct expected-value analysis by assigning probabilities to different barrel-production scenarios for each region
Assess political stability and legal frameworks in each country
Obtain insurance cost estimates for each region
Negotiate hedging contracts to protect against oil price downside below the breakeven threshold
